items.title: Seven Kinds of Practitioner and the Objects Suited to Each

items.zh: 又於此中，貪、瞋、癡、慢尋思行者，彼先應於淨行所緣淨修其行，然後方證心正安住。彼於各別所緣境界，定由所緣差別勢力，勤修加行。若等分行補特伽羅，隨所愛樂，攀緣彼境勤修加行。如是勤修，唯令心住，非淨其行。如等分行補特伽羅，薄塵行者，當知亦爾。
items.en: Further, in this matter, practitioners dominated by desire, aversion, delusion, pride, or discursive thought should first purify their own conduct using the purifying objects, and only then attain the mind's correct settling. … A practitioner of balanced temperament, following whatever they find agreeable, engages that object and diligently applies effort; such diligent practice serves only to settle the mind, not to purify conduct. As with the practitioner of balanced temperament, so too should one understand the practitioner of naturally light affliction.

items.zh: 而彼諸行，有其差別。謂貪等行者勤修行時，要經久遠，方證心住。

items.title: Balanced and Light-Affliction Practitioners; the Three Obstructions

items.zh: 等分行者勤修行時，不甚久遠，能證心住。薄塵行者勤修行時，最極速疾，能證心住。問：前已廣說有貪等行補特伽羅行相差別，其等分行及薄塵行補特伽羅，有何行相？答：等分行者，如貪等行補特伽羅所有行相，一切具有；然彼行相非上、非勝，如貪等行。隨所遇緣，有其差別，施設此行與彼相似。其薄塵行補特伽羅行相差別者，謂無重障，最初清淨，資糧已具，多清淨信，成就聰慧，具諸福德，具諸功德。無重障者，謂無三障。何等為三？一者、業障，二、煩惱障，三、異熟障。言業障者：謂五無間業，及餘所有故思造業諸尤重業。彼異熟果若成就時，能障正道，令不生起。是名業障。
items.en: A practitioner of balanced temperament, diligently practising, attains the mind's settling in not too long a time. A practitioner of naturally light affliction, diligently practising, attains it with the greatest speed. … The distinguishing marks of the practitioner of naturally light affliction are these: freedom from serious obstruction; purity from the very start; the provisions already complete; abundant pure faith; accomplished intelligence; possession of merit; and possession of virtue. Freedom from serious obstruction means freedom from three obstructions. What are the three? Karmic obstruction, afflictive obstruction, and retributive obstruction. Karmic obstruction is the five acts of immediate retribution, together with any other especially grave deliberately-committed karma. When their ripened result matures, it is able to obstruct the correct path, preventing it from arising — this is called karmic obstruction.

items.title: Section: Affliction and Ripened-Result Close the Three Obstructions

items.zh: 煩惱障者，謂猛利煩惱、長時煩惱。由此煩惱，於現法中，以其種種淨行所緣不能令淨，是名煩惱障。異熟障者，謂若生處，聖道依彼不生不長，於是生處異熟果生。或有生處，聖道依彼雖得生長，而於其中異熟果生，聾騃愚鈍，盲瞽瘖瘂，以手代言，無有力能解了善說、惡說法義。是名異熟障。
items.en: Afflictive obstruction is affliction that is either fierce or long-lasting. Because of such affliction, in this present life, none of the various purifying objects of meditation are able to purify the mind — this is called afflictive obstruction. Retributive obstruction is: either being born into circumstances where the noble path cannot arise or grow at all, the ripened result of that birth itself being the obstruction; or being born where the path could in principle arise and grow, yet the ripened result manifests as deafness, dullness, blindness, or muteness — reduced to gesture in place of speech, without the capacity to understand either well-taught or poorly-taught teachings. This is called retributive obstruction.

items.title: Purity from the Start: Well-Purified Discipline and an Upright View

items.zh: 最初清淨者，謂善淨戒及正直見。由十因緣，戒善清淨，如前應知。正直見者，謂若有見，淨信相應故、勝解相應故、遠離誑諂故、善思法義無惑無疑加行出離故，名為正直。如是正直見，淨信相應故，於佛正法及毘奈耶不可引奪。
items.en: Purity from the very start means well-purified discipline together with an upright view. An upright view is one accompanied by pure faith, accompanied by resolute understanding, free of deceit and flattery, and skilfully considering the meaning of the teaching without confusion or doubt, applying effort towards genuine release — this is called upright. Such an upright view, being accompanied by pure faith, cannot be drawn away from the Buddha's true teaching and discipline.

items.title: Section: Resolute Understanding of the Inconceivable Closes Purity from the Start

items.zh: 勝解相應故，於諸如來及聖弟子不可思議威德神力、不可思議生處差別、甚深法教、不可記事，深生勝解，無驚、無恐、無有怖畏。遠離誑諂故，其見正直，是正直類，如其聖教而正修行，如其真實而自現發。善思法義無惑無疑加行出離故，於一切法無常、苦、空、無我等義，善正思惟、善正籌量、善正觀察。由是為因，無惑無疑，遠離二路，逮得昇進。由此四相，先所說見，名正直見。
items.en: Being accompanied by resolute understanding, one generates deep resolute understanding — free of alarm, free of fear, free of dread — regarding the inconceivable majestic power of the Tathāgatas and noble disciples, the inconceivable differences in beings' births and the places they inhabit, the profound teaching, and the matters the Buddha left unanswered. Being free of deceit and flattery, one's view is upright, of an upright kind, practising correctly in accordance with the noble teaching and manifesting genuinely just as one has actually realised. Skilfully considering the meaning of the teaching without confusion or doubt and applying effort towards release, one skilfully and correctly reflects, deliberates, and observes the meaning of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self in all phenomena; by this cause, free of confusion and doubt, one departs from the two divergent paths of wavering and attains genuine advancement. Through these four marks, the view spoken of earlier is called an upright view.

items.title: The Provisions Already Complete: Merit and Wisdom

items.zh: 資糧已具者，廣說資糧，如前應知。略有四種。一、福德資糧，二、智慧資糧，三、先世資糧，四、現法資糧。福德資糧者，謂由此故，於今獲得隨順資具、豐饒財寶，遇真福田為善知識，離諸障礙，能勤修行。智慧資糧者，謂由此故，成就聰慧，有力有能解了善說、惡說法義，獲得隨順法教、義教、教授教誡。
items.en: The provisions already complete are, in detail, the provisions explained earlier — briefly, four kinds: the provision of merit, the provision of wisdom, the provision from past lives, and the provision within this present life. The provision of merit is that through which one now obtains fitting requisites and abundant wealth, encounters a genuine field of merit as a spiritual friend, and is free of obstruction, able to diligently practice. The provision of wisdom is that through which one becomes accomplished in intelligence, having the capacity to understand both well-taught and poorly-taught teachings, and obtains what accords with the teaching itself, its meaning, and instruction and admonition.

items.zh: 先世資糧者，謂由宿世積集善根，於今獲得諸根成就。

blocks.text: How different temperaments progress, three kinds of obstruction, and the marks of one whose afflictions are light.

Those dominated by desire, aversion, delusion, pride, or discursive thought "should first purify their own conduct using the purifying objects, and only then attain the mind's settling". Venerable Miào Jìng: the aim is simply to settle the mind. The balanced type settles "in not too long a time"; the lightly afflicted, quickly.

**Karmic**: the five heinous deeds and other grave deliberate wrongs. **Afflictive**: affliction "either fierce or long-lasting", so that no purifying object helps in this life. **Retributive**: born where the noble path cannot arise.
The lightly afflicted have "well-purified discipline together with an upright view", a view "accompanied by pure faith" that cannot be drawn away from the true teaching.

They have "deep resolute understanding, free of alarm or fear, regarding the inconceivable majestic power of the Buddhas". Venerable Miào Jìng asks why a mountain has the shape it has: some things simply are as they are.
Four provisions: of merit, of wisdom, from past lives, and in this life.

quiz.q: A balanced practitioner chooses any agreeable object. What is the aim, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only to settle the mind, not to purify it — unlike those with a dominant affliction
quiz.why: "Such diligent practice serves only to settle the mind, not to purify conduct." Venerable Miào Jìng: the aim is simply to settle the mind, not to purify it — unlike the earlier case of a dominant affliction.

quiz.q: Those dominated by an affliction should first purify conduct. How does Master Cháng Bǎi say to begin?
options: first see which affliction is heaviest and prescribe for it
quiz.why: "Should first purify their own conduct using the purifying objects, and only then attain the mind's correct settling." Master Cháng Bǎi: first observe which affliction is heaviest in oneself, and prescribe according to it.

quiz.q: Karmic obstruction is the five immediate deeds and other grave deliberate karma. Why is it an obstruction, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: other karma may be transformed or lightened; this kind hardly can — hence an obstruction
quiz.why: "Karmic obstruction is the five acts of immediate retribution, together with any other especially grave deliberately-committed karma." Master Cháng Bǎi: other karma may be transformed — heavy retribution received lightly — but this kind is very hard to transform; it becomes an obstruction.

quiz.q: Afflictive obstruction is "fierce affliction, long-lasting affliction." The English says "either," the note says "both at once." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: long-lasting but milder affliction is also an obstruction; Cháng Bǎi: even lower-grade affliction arising long is one, growing into middle and upper
quiz.why: "Afflictive obstruction is affliction that is either fierce or long-lasting." Venerable Miào Jìng: the second is long-lasting affliction — not so heavy, but long. Master Cháng Bǎi: lower-grade affliction arising over a long time is also an obstruction, since lower gives rise to middle and middle to upper. The note's "both at once" conflicts with the lectures.

quiz.q: What is "purity from the very start," and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say of discipline and right view?
options: well-purified discipline and an upright view; discipline keeps one from every fault, right view is the root of boundless merit
quiz.why: "Purity from the very start means well-purified discipline together with an upright view." Venerable Miào Jìng: discipline is what keeps one from every fault; right view is the root from which boundless merit is accomplished.

quiz.q: "不可思議生處差別" is rendered "the inconceivable variety of realms of rebirth." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: following the Pixunji: the differences of the sentient and physical worlds — why a mountain looks as it does is not to be speculated on
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: why is this mountain shaped like this rather than some other way? Following the Pixunji he reads 生處差別 as the differences of the physical and sentient worlds; the English and the note lean towards details of rebirth.

quiz.q: How many kinds of provisions are there, and who does Venerable Miào Jìng say the "genuine field of merit" is?
options: four — merit, wisdom, past lives, present life; the genuine field is the noble ones, first through fourth fruit
quiz.why: "Briefly, four kinds: the provision of merit, the provision of wisdom, the provision from past lives, and the provision within this present life." Venerable Miào Jìng: meeting a genuine field of merit — the genuine field should be said to be the noble ones, those of the first through fourth fruits.
